extracted.intended_audience: fact-checking organizations and journalists seeking IFCN signatory status
extracted.subtask_short: IFCN Code of Principles signatory criteria
extracted.subtask_description: High-level requirements and expectations for organizations that want to become signatories to the International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN) Code of Principles, emphasizing transparency, nonpartisanship, and assessor qualifications. The page is an overview and points to fuller criteria and the application process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to Transparency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page heading and core commitment. The page positions transparency as a central obligation for signatories; it links to 'Become a Signatory' and 'See the Criteria' for details but does not enumerate specific transparency practices on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisan and transparent fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: We believe nonpartisan and transparent fact-checking can be a powerful instrument of accountable journalism; conversely, unsourced or biased fact-checking can increase distrust in the media and experts while polluting public understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as a normative principle: fact-checking must be both nonpartisan and transparent. The page frames these as necessary to preserve public trust and accurate public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing and avoidance of bias (no unsourced or biased fact-checking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsourced or biased fact-checking can increase distrust in the media and experts while polluting public understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit evaluative criterion: fact-checks should be sourced and free from bias. While the page doesn't list specific sourcing rules, it warns that unsourced or biased work is harmful and therefore contrary to the Code's commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for fact-checking capacity (networking, capacity building, collaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: We enable fact-checkers through networking, capacity building, and collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as part of IFCN's mission and signatory benefits/expectations: the network provides support to improve fact-checking work. Not an evaluation metric per se, but an offered commitment and likely part of the signatory relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external assessors with relevant expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: External assessors are journalism professors, researchers or media consultants with knowledge of fact-checking, transparency, and political context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for how signatory applications are evaluated: assessments are performed by external experts with specified backgrounds and topical knowledge. This communicates assessor qualifications and the evaluative body for applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and membership requirements referenced (see the Criteria / See the process)
rubrics_metrics.description: The commitments of the Code of Principles — See what it takes to become a member. Application Process — Ready to get started with your application? Learn more about the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to fuller, detailed criteria and an application process but does not include those details here. The presence of these links implies procedural and documentary requirements for signatory status (e.g., application materials, evidence of adherence), which must be consulted on the linked pages.
